span.label: method
span.quote: We develop an algorithm that can detect pneumonia from chest X-rays at a level exceeding practicing radiologists.

span.label: pneumonia detection on chest radiographs
span.quote: However, detecting pneumonia in chest X-rays is a challenging task that relies on the availability of expert radiologists.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: CheXNet is a 121-layer Dense Convolutional Network (DenseNet) (Huang et al., 2016) trained on the ChestX-ray 14 dataset.

span.label: the paper identifies three limitations of its radiologist comparison
span.quote: We identify three limitations of this comparison.

span.label: The paper announces three limitations of the radiologist comparison but enumerates only two (a 'First' and a 'Third'); the second is missing from the text.
span.quote: We identify three limitations of this comparison.

span.label: Only frontal radiographs were shown to both model and radiologists, although a share of accurate diagnoses requires the lateral view.
span.quote: First, only frontal radiographs were presented to the radiologists and model during diagnosis, but it has been shown that up to 15% of accurate diagnoses require the lateral view (Raoof et al., 2012); we thus expect that this setup provides a conservative estimate of performance.

span.label: Neither model nor radiologists could use patient history, which is known to change radiologist diagnostic performance.
span.quote: Third, neither the model nor the radiologists were not permitted to use patient history, which has been shown to decrease radiologist diagnostic performance in interpreting chest radiographs (Berbaum et al., 1985; Potchen et al., 1979);

span.label: The standard the model is measured against is the other radiologists' labels, not the presence of disease.
span.quote: We compute the F1 score for each individual radiologist and for CheXNet against each of the other 4 labels as ground truth

span.label: The training labels were produced by text extraction from reports rather than by anyone looking at the images.
span.quote: annotate each image with up to 14 different thoracic pathology labels using automatic extraction methods on radiology reports

span.label: Every image the extractor did not mark becomes a negative example.
span.quote: We label images that have pneumonia as one of the annotated pathologies as positive examples and label all other images as negative examples

span.label: The model reports fourteen findings while the headline number describes one of them.
span.quote: instead of outputting one binary label, ChexNet outputs a vector t of binary labels indicating the absence or presence of each of the following 14 pathology classes

span.label: a deep convolutional network (DenseNet) applied to detect disease from chest X-rays at radiologist level
span.quote: a 121-layer convolutional neural network trained on ChestX-ray14

span.label: 'exceeding practicing radiologists' - AS AGREEMENT WITH FOUR OF THEM: the F1 for the model and for each radiologist is computed against the other four radiologists' labels, so the claim is about concordance with a particular panel and not about detecting pneumonia in a patient
span.quote: We compute the F1 score for each individual radiologist and for CheXNet against each of the other 4 labels as ground truth

span.label: a pathology label - AS A FACT ABOUT A REPORT, NOT AN IMAGE: the fourteen labels are assigned by automatic extraction from radiology reports, so the target the network learns is what a radiologist wrote down, filtered through a text-mining tool
span.quote: annotate each image with up to 14 different thoracic pathology labels using automatic extraction methods on radiology reports

span.label: 'negative' - AS NOT-LABELLED: every image without pneumonia among its annotated pathologies becomes a negative example, so the class means the extractor found nothing rather than that nothing was there
span.quote: We label images that have pneumonia as one of the annotated pathologies as positive examples and label all other images as negative examples
